correctness.rationale: Longitude orthogonality gives the signed-order blocks; each pure degree has half its norm on the hemisphere, and m=±(ℓ+1) gives singleton blocks. The normalized Legendre Lagrange identity gives the signed overlap as the boundary Wronskian at 0 divided by 2(ℓ+1); the t=1 term vanishes (m=0 is smooth; for m≥1 the factors have endpoint order m/2). For j+m=2r, j-m=2s the normalized value at zero has modulus √((2j+1)B_r B_s/2). For j+m=2r-1, j-m=2s-1 the normalized derivative has modulus √((2j+1)(2r)(2s)B_r B_s/2). Adjacent degrees have matching signs in the value–derivative product in the even case and opposite signs in the reversed product in the odd case, giving positive overlap in both. Along with (2r+2)B_(r+1)=(2r+1)B_r this yields exactly the frozen F/G formulas and factors. Strict Cauchy–Schwarz on [0,1] bounds each overlap below 1/2, since neither factor is proportional to the other on an open interval. The strictly increasing ratios F_(j+1)/F_j, with F₀=1, give F_r F_s<F_(r+s) when r,s>0. Wallis gives G_r G_s<2/π<√(2/π)<F_ℓ, so only |m|=ℓ attains the maximum. Signs give the plus-combinations in the stipulated convention, with a single line at ℓ=0 (whose overlap is √3/4). The exact ratio of adjacent top gaps is √((2ℓ+3)(2ℓ+5))/(2ℓ+4), and the 1/(8ℓ) correction follows by expanding the factorial expression. The frozen checker and verification notes were inspected, not executed; finite quadrature does not prove the all-degree claims.

value.rationale: Sharp concentration for a fixed two-degree band is a natural and potentially useful spectral problem. But the exact invariant, its optimizers and its quantitative large-degree behavior are all evaluated in a stronger matching record. The only possible isolated addendum, a consecutive ratio, is obtained by canceling consecutive central binomial coefficients in the existing formula; it has no independent mathematical contribution here. No repair to a surviving valuable finding is supported.
